sentences.text:
These appeals are filed against the judgment and award of the Tribunal dated 08.08.2024 passed by IV Additional Small Causes and Additional MACT, Bangalore in MVC No.2589/2020.
3.

entities.text: IV Additional Small Causes and Additional MACT, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The brief of the case is that on 02.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m. when the petitioner was riding his Honda shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EZ-3441 along with his friend Akasha as his pillion rider on the extreme left side of Bengaluru-Gowribidanur SH-9 road from Bengaluru side, near Allipura Cross, Thondebhavi Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk, driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-825 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following any traffic rules and regulations from ACC cement factory side towards SH-9 road and dashed against motor cycle.
Due to impact, petitioner and pillion rider were thrown out from the motor cycle and sustained severe head and bodily injuries and petitioner's motor cycle damaged extensively.

Immediately petitioner and pillion rider were shifted in 108 ambulance to NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR Gowribidanur Govt. hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and shifted to Bangalore Baptist hospital, Bangalore and admitted him as inpatient on 03.06.2020.
The petitioner has stated that he is suffering from disability and discomforts and spent huge money for his treatment.
4. The injured claimant, who is aged 30 years has met with an accident on 02.06.2020 and filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.45,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.34,72,338/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

5. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award of the Tribunal, the Insurance Company has preferred an appeal in MFA No.6639/2024 and mainly contented that the Tribunal has awarded excessive compensation.
It is further contended that the insured has not complied with the provisions of 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act and that the lorry was not involved in the alleged accident.

It is also urged that there is no evidence regarding negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and NC:
2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR that the claimant himself contributed to the accident to the extent of 50%,
as he was not wearing a helmet and did not posses a valid driving licence.
6.

It is further contended that the claimant was working as a Generator Mechanic at Sine Wave Generators Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, and has failed to produce any bank statement to substantiate his alleged monthly income of Rs.23,900/-, nor has he filed any Income Tax Returns.

Despite the same,
the Tribunal has erroneously taken his monthly income at Rs.23,900/- without deducting professional tax.
The Tribunal has granted more compensation under the head of pain and suffering, loss of income during laid-up period, loss of future amenities and medical expenses.
Therefore, the Insurance Company prays for reduction of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
7. The injured claimant has also filed MFA No. 3507/2025 for enhancement of compensation against the same judgment and award.
It is contended that after the accident, the claimant remained hospitalized as an inpatient for a total period of 196 days.

During the course of treatment, he NC:
2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR underwent surgery, namely open reduction performed at the diaphyseal fracture site due to maluniting fracture and closed reduction achieved under Orthopaedic Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Nagabhushana Reddy on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126949403/
4 department.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further stated that claimant was aged 30 years at the time of the accident and was working as a Generator Mechanic in Sine Wave Generator Pvt. Ltd., earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
PW.2-Doctor assessed the whole-body physical disability at 18%, mental disability at 10% and total permanent disability at 26%.
However, the Tribunal has erred in considering the permanent disability at only 15%.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of the compensation.
9. It is stated that the claimant has produced the salary slip at Ex.P10, which discloses that his gross salary was Rs.23,900/- per month and net pay was Rs.21,979/- per month.
The Tribunal after deducting the compulsory deductions, has taken at Rs.23,700/- and it needs no interference.

The claimant was aged 30 years and the multiplier applied is '16'.
NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR 10.

As per Ex.P4 - the wound certificate, the claimant sustained the following injuries:
"(1) petitioner was unconscious, swelling only, occipital region present, lacerated wound over left temporal region 2 x 2 cm present (2) cm present (2) fracture of right leg present (3) fracture of right little finger present (4) multiple abrasions over right knee and dorsum of both hands present"
11.

Exs.P7 to P9 are three discharge summaries, which disclose that the claimant was admitted in the hospital for a total period of 196 days and that he underwent surgery, namely, open reduction at the diaphyseal fracture site due to a malunited fracture, and closed reduction was achieved under the Orthopaedic Department.

12. PW2-Doctor stated that the claimant sustained head injury, facial bone fracture, fracture neck of right femur, type I open fracture femur shaft, right patella fracture, right tibia fracture, dislocation of the 5th metacarpal with right NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR hemiparesis.

He further stated that the claimant was treated under ICU care and medications for the head injury and open reduction and internal fixation with recon nail on 24.06.2020 and fracture of the right tibia was treated conservatively and discharged on 23.07.2020.
13.
It is further stated that the claimant was again admitted to another hospital for physiotherapy from 16.10.2020 to 26.12.2020.
PW.2 further stated that the claimant now complains of weakness in right side of the body, unable to walk independently, need support and assistance.
The petitioner walks with walker restricted right hip and knee movements, wasting of the right lower limb muscles.
PW.2 assessed whole body whole-body physical disability at 18%, mental disability at 10% and total permanent disability at 26%.
However, the Tribunal has considered the disability at only 15%.
14. The date of birth of the claimant is 08.06.1989 and the date of the accident is 02.06.2021.

As such, the claimant was aged 30 years, 11 months, and 24 days at the time of the accident and was about to complete 31 years within a short Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Nagabhushana Reddy on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126949403/
5 - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR span and thus, the multiplier is to be taken as '16'.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Nagabhushana Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take the functional disability at '20%'.
The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the age of the claimant ought to be taken as 30 years and the appropriate multiplier as '17'.
However, this Court finds it just and proper to take the age of the claimant as 31 years and apply the multiplier of '16'.
Accordingly, the 'loss of future earning capacity' is comes to Rs.23,700/-  12  16  20%=Rs.9,10,080/-.
This Court further finds that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is reasonable and needs no interference.

15. Thus in all, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of future earning capacity 9,10,080/-
 (23,700 x 12 x 16 x 20%)

2 Pain and suffering 2,00,000  3. Loss of income during laid up 2,37,000  period  4. Attendant charges, transportation 1,50,000  and nourishment  - 11 -  NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR  5. Loss of amenities, medical 1,00,000  expenses  6.
Medical expenses 20,42,778  7.
Future Medical Expenses 60,000
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.34,72,338/- but the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.37,00,000/-.
Therefore the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,27,662/- (Rs.37,00,000/- - Rs.34,72,338/-).

17. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
MFA No. 3507/2025 is allowed-in-part.

- 12 - NC: 2026:KHC:7118 HC-KAR iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
 iv.
Draw award accordingly.
v. The disability is assessed at 20%, as it affects the claimant's ability to attend to his day-to-day activities.
Accordingly, MFA No.6639/2024 filed by the insurance company stands dismissed.
